mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the simultaneous state where Team A's recent shots FOR (RECENT_5) exceeds its ALL_PRIOR shots FOR, AND Team A's recent shots_on_target FOR (RECENT_5) exceeds its ALL_PRIOR shots_on_target FOR, AND Team B's recent shots AGAINST (RECENT_5) exceeds its ALL_PRIOR shots AGAINST. Measure corner_kicks and shots_on_target outcomes in matches satisfying all three conditions jointly.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When all three conditions hold simultaneously, Team A's corner_kicks FOR and shots_on_target FOR rise together relative to baseline — the joint uplift is larger than the sum of each single-observable uplift.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has risen sharply in recent matches while its shots-on-target conversion rate (shots on target as a share of total shots) has also improved recently, yet Team B concedes more shots in recent matches than its season average. The joint relationship between Team A's recent shot volume uplift AND its recent on-target accuracy uplift, set against Team B's recent defensive shot-concession trend, may jointly predict corner and on-target activity beyond what either observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the simultaneous joint state of three distinct observables across two teams — Team A's shot volume trend, Team A's accuracy trend, and Team B's defensive shot-concession trend — none of which can be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split corner_kicks FOR (Team A) and corner_kicks AGAINST (Team B) by half. Condition on the cross-team, cross-half joint state: compare Team A's first-half corner production rate against Team B's first-half corner concession rate, and separately Team A's second-half corner production rate against Team B's second-half corner concession rate. Test whether the half-level pairing reveals a divergent within-match trajectory.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's corner production relative to Team B's concession rate is lower in the first half and rises in the second half — the within-match trajectory is non-flat and the half-level joint pairing diverges from the full-match average pairing.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner_kicks FOR are split asymmetrically across halves (first-half mean notably lower than second-half mean), while Team B's corner_kicks AGAINST are also split across halves. The joint half-level corner production of Team A against Team B's half-level corner concession profile may reveal a within-match timing asymmetry in corner activity that a full-match view obscures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) split applied jointly across two teams' asymmetric observables — it requires both the half resolution and the cross-team pairing simultaneously, which is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint half-level state: Team A's goals AGAINST FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF split, paired with Team B's goals FOR FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF split. Test whether the half in which Team A is most vulnerable (first) aligns or misaligns with the half in which Team B is most productive (second), and measure how total goals in each half relate to this cross-team timing asymmetry.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The cross-team half-level pairing reveals a timing mismatch — Team A's defensive vulnerability peak (first half) does not coincide with Team B's attacking output peak (second half) — such that the joint half-level profile diverges from a flat within-match distribution implied by full-match averages alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A concedes goals heavily in the first half (high first-half goals AGAINST) relative to the second half, while Team B scores more goals in the second half than the first half. This cross-team, cross-half asymmetry in goal-scoring timing — where Team A's defensive vulnerability is concentrated in the first half but Team B's attacking output is concentrated in the second half — creates a joint within-match state that differs from what either team's full-match goal average implies.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires simultaneously conditioning on two teams' half-level splits for the same observable (goals) in an asymmetric cross-team pairing — not reducible to one observable with one band, and requires half-level data resolution.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where both Team A's possession FOR and Team B's possession FOR are below 50% (both sides are sub-50% possession teams). Within this joint condition, measure fouls FOR/AGAINST and yellow_cards FOR/AGAINST and cards_2h, comparing against the competition context baseline and against matches where at least one team holds majority possession.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams are structurally sub-50% possession sides, fouls and yellow_cards are elevated relative to the competition context baseline, and cards_2h are also elevated — the joint low-possession pairing is associated with a more contested, card-prone match profile.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession is structurally below 50% (both all-prior and recent), while Team B also operates below 50% possession on average. When both teams in a match are sub-50% possession sides, the joint low-possession context may be associated with a distinct foul and card profile — specifically elevated fouls and cards — compared to matches where at least one team dominates possession. Team B concedes notably more fouls than the competition average, reinforcing this joint dynamic.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint condition of two distinct observables (possession for each team) both falling below a threshold simultaneously — a two-dimensional threshold condition across two teams — not reducible to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's shots_on_target FOR rate (shots_on_target / shots) is below competition average AND Team B's shots_on_target FOR rate is at or above competition average. Within this asymmetric joint condition, measure total shots_on_target in the match and compare against matches where both teams have similar shot-quality profiles.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A has a structurally lower shot-to-on-target conversion rate than Team B, the match-level shots_on_target distribution is asymmetric — Team B generates a disproportionately higher share of total match shots_on_target relative to its share of total shots, and this asymmetry is larger than what either team's individual shot-quality profile alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shots FOR have a low conversion to shots_on_target (shots_on_target FOR as a share of shots FOR is well below competition average), while Team B's shots_on_target AGAINST are also below competition average. The joint relationship between Team A's low shot accuracy and Team B's low shot-on-target concession rate creates a compounded suppression of on-target activity that is asymmetric: Team B's own shots_on_target FOR are above competition average, meaning the two teams have opposing shot-quality profiles. This cross-team asymmetry in shot quality (accuracy FOR vs accuracy AGAINST) is a joint two-observable, two-team relationship.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint cross-team comparison of two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for both teams simultaneously, forming an asymmetric two-team, two-observable relationship — not reducible to one observable with one conditioning band.
